personality: Bright, trusting and quick to learn. She is fooled once and never again.
voice: I will never leave the path again.

cards.title: The Red Cap
cards.text: There was once a sweet little girl who was loved by everyone who saw her, and most of all by her grandmother, who could not give her enough. One day the grandmother gave her a little cap of red velvet. It suited her so well that she would wear nothing else, and so everyone called her Little Red-Cap.

source.author: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, 1812–57; English by Margaret Hunt, 1884

cards.title: The Path Through the Wood
cards.text: Her mother sent her through the wood with cake and wine for her grandmother, who was ill, and told her not to leave the path. A wolf met her and talked her into picking flowers. When she reached the cottage he was already in her grandmother's bed, and he swallowed her whole. A passing huntsman cut him open, and out she came, saying how dark it had been inside.

source.author: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, 1812–57; English by Margaret Hunt, 1884

cards.title: Never Again
cards.text: Afterwards she promised herself she would never leave the path again. Some time later another wolf spoke to her in the wood, and this time she hurried straight to her grandmother's and told her. They bolted the door. The wolf climbed onto the roof to wait for her, so they filled the trough below with water that sausages had been boiled in. The smell drew him down; he slipped and drowned.

source.author: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, 1812–57; English by Margaret Hunt, 1884
